title: Matchability-Aware Conformal Prediction for Open-Ended Language Model Generation
claim: Sampling clarifications and weighting by aleatoric versus epistemic uncertainty gives coverage sets, but coverage is capped by whether the answer was ever sampled.
layout: 2 stacked panels; top 3 columns by 5 numbered steps, top-to-bottom arrow; bottom theorem
description: The figure has two boxed panels. The top panel, titled 'CAELUM on three example queries', has three columns: an ambiguous query (teal) and two knowledge-gap queries (purple). Five numbered steps run down the page on a vertical arrow: query, clarify/sample/cluster, uncertainty, prediction set, output. Step 2 shows rows of colored dots for sampled answers by cluster. Step 3 shows teal and purple horizontal bars for U_ale and U_epi, with the weight w computed under each. Step 4 shows tables of answer clusters with probabilities, cumulative mass and a dashed threshold line. Step 5 shows a green check for 'covered' and a red X for 'missed'. The bottom panel, 'Matchability caps coverage', shows grids of blue and red-X squares split by a classifier, plus Theorem 1 with its inequality and a numeric bound.
caption: Method overview. Each top-panel column shows the same five steps. Disagreement between clarifications raises $\Uale$, and disagreement within a clarification raises $\Uepi$. The weight $w$ sets the effective threshold $\eta=\min\{\hat\tau w,1\}$ for selecting clusters in [ref]. The third column's reference answer is absent from sampled support, so expanding the set cannot include it. The lower panel shows the matchability bound. Main experiments use $n=5$ and kernel entropy.
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) often do not produce calibrated uncertainty estimates for their answers. We propose CAELUM, a framework that builds semantic prediction sets while separating aleatoric from epistemic uncertainty. CAELUM samples answers using an ensemble of clarification prompts, clusters them by semantic equivalence, and estimates the aleatoric and epistemic components via kernel-based von Neumann entropy before calibrating nonconformity scores with split conformal prediction. We use a weight $w_Î»(x)=1+U_{\mathrm{ale}}(x)+Î»\,U_{\mathrm{epi}}(x)$ to control for the contribution of the epistemic uncertainty of each instance and fit a coefficient $Î»^\star$ to minimize prediction set size. When the objective is nonflat and selection is stable across splits, $Î»^\star$ could be a diagnostic, where large values may indicate epistemic dominance (retrieve, abstain) and $Î»^\star\to 0$ aleatoric dominance (clarify). For individual queries, a log ratio $R(x)$ compares the weighted epistemic component with the aleatoric component. Theoretically, we demonstrate that the coverage is capped by matchability, the fraction of items whose reference answer appears in any sampled cluster. Empirically, this matchability can be predicted from the original question features using a lightweight classifier. We use those predictions to define a stratum and derive a conformal coverage bound within it. Across 30 LLM and dataset combinations (4-32B), mean coverage is 0.74 in the learned stratum versus 0.65 overall, averaged over the 78 evaluations using the learned classifier.
